LESSON: READING 15.2.1 READING FLUENCY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 15
Topic 15.2: Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency, part of Strand 15 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can you tell if a text is appropriate for reading? 2. Why should one read a text fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. preview a text while ignoring unknown words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make predictions about the characters, events and the message in a given text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. skim a text to get the gist,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. scan a text to obtain specific information

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. advocate the role of reading fluency in communication. • Watch videos of a text being read. Learners with postural limitations could be preferentially positioned for enhanced viewing. • Read the title, blurb of a text in pairs. • Read the first line of a paragraph or chapter to establish the subject. • Look for specific details from a text such as tittle, a word, a phrase in pairs. • Practise ignoring unknown words while reading. 1. How can you tell if a text is appropriate for reading? 2. Why should one read a text fluently? 153 • Practise timed reading in groups with fluency. Consider purposive grouping for this activity and allow more time for learners with speech difficulties. • Read a text on tourist attraction sites in the world at the right speed. Learners who may not turn pages to use page-turners or be supported by peers. • Pronounce words and sounds accurately. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip-read by the teacher or peers. • Display the right emotions and feelings when reading a text. • Record a text such as a poem, a story or newspaper article and save the recording in a digital device. 154

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 15.2.1 Reading Fluency together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

Communication and collaboration is fostered as the learner develops reading fluency

Values
